title: What does each child get when 3 rotis are shared among 4 children?
description: Each of the three rotis is cut into four equal pieces, and each child takes three pieces. The share is then written as a division fact, an addition fact and a multiplication fact, and checked by counting all the pieces.
teaching_notes: One idea: three rotis shared among four children gives three fourths of a roti each, because each roti is cut into four equal pieces. Watch for students who say each child gets three rotis or one roti.

source: Figure it Out Q1 (section 7.6, second block)
video_script.why: A learner finds the share when three rotis are shared equally among four children and writes the division, addition and multiplication facts.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own rotis shared among four children
video_script.anchor: three rotis on a table and four children waiting to share them
video_script.payoff_line: Each child gets three quarters of a roti

final_answer.value: Each child gets 3/4 roti. Division fact: 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4. Addition fact: 3 = 3/4 + 3/4 + 3/4 + 3/4. Multiplication fact: 3 = 4 × 3/4.
final_answer.spoken: each child gets three quarters of a roti, with the division, addition and multiplication facts

maths_rules: 3 rotis among 4 children: cut each roti into 4 equal pieces, giving 12 pieces
12 pieces among 4 children is 3 pieces each, and one piece is 1/4 roti, so each child gets 3/4 roti
check: 4 children with 3 pieces each use 12 pieces, which is all of the 3 rotis
video_script.design: One idea: cut every roti into as many pieces as there are children. The three rotis stay on the table and the cut pieces move to the children.
